summary: Config guidance: graceful throttle fallbacks for mixed webhook + embed warmup traffic
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Lightbeam Analytics reports intermittent 429 errors during a scheduled warmup that mixes high-rate embedding backfills with real-time webhook callbacks. Their ingest pipeline runs a parallel warmup job that pins a model variant and at the same time they receive webhook-driven requests for scoring; throttles appear opaque and customer is unsure which rate pool is being exhausted.

Impact:
- Multiple 429s for a subset of webhook callbacks and embedding push requests between 03:00 - 03:20 UTC during daily warmup window.
- Client saw ~12% of webhook calls failing with 429s, causing downstream retries and duplication.
- This is a dedicated customer using reserved capacity; they expect warmup to not interfere with realtime webhook SLA.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (us-east)
- Prod tenant: lightbeam-prod (dedicated)
- Model pin: open-llama-7b / text-embedding-ada-002 for embeddings
- Ingest pattern: 50 parallel warmup workers (cron) + webhook fans from external partners (~40 concurrent short streams)

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Schedule a warmup job that sends n=50 concurrent embed init requests over 10 minutes to pin the model.
2) Simultaneously fire webhook callback traffic at ~40 concurrent short sessions using ephemeral keys.
3) Observe 429s on webhook endpoints and some embed push retries.

Relevant logs/headers (redacted):
- Upstream response sample: 429 {"retry_after": null, "reason": "route_quota_exhausted"}
- Throttle headers observed: X-RateLimit-Limit: 10000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Window: 60s (inconsistent across requests)
- Customer notes backend shows some warmup workers reuse same ephemeral API key causing fanout amplification.

Customer ask:
- Clarify which quota layers (route vs tenant vs connection) are being applied for: 1) long-lived embedding warmup requests and 2) webhook short sessions using ephemeral keys.
- Recommend configuration changes (burst pools, route isolation, priority lanes) for dedicated pools so warmup does not cause webhook 429s.
- Temporary mitigation steps they can apply immediately while we investigate telemetry.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:14 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Acked ticket, requested full request/response samples and representative timestamps. Escalated to SRE for rate-limiter traces.
2026-03-12 10:03 UTC - Customer (Lightbeam): Provided sample request IDs and a short trace window. Noted that ephemeral keys are minted via their orchestrator and have high fanout.

2026-03-12 13:22 UTC - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Pulled rate-limiter traces for tenant lightbeam-prod between 03:00-03:30 UTC. Observed token-window drop concentrated on route /v1/embeddings/push and intermittent per-connection counters for websocket endpoints. Hypothesis: warmup workers and webhook sessions are sharing tenant burst credits in the dedicated pool; ephemeral key reuse amplified counts.

2026-03-13 08:45 UTC - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Suggested short-term mitigations: 1) add a dedicated priority class for webhook routes (priority=high) with isolated burst pool; 2) reduce concurrency of warmup workers to 10-15 simultaneous clients and add jitter; 3) switch warmup requests to a non-urgent traffic class or schedule outside webhook peak window.

2026-03-14 11:30 UTC - Customer (Lightbeam): Implemented warmup concurrency limit and enabled route isolation for webhooks. Reported success — webhook 429s dropped to <1% during next warmup run. Asked for follow-up doc on recommended default settings for dedicated customers running mixed workloads.
2026-03-14 16:05 UTC - Support (Aisha): Confirmed customer success and opened follow-up to deliver configuration guidance doc and checklist. Marked ticket to remain open until guidance delivered.
investigation_notes: Rate-limiter trace extraction (03:00-03:20 UTC): tenant token bucket shows large bursts consumed by embedding warmup traffic. The warmup client re-used a small set of ephemeral keys causing per-key multiplexing counts to aggregate at the tenant layer.

Observed fallback behavior: when route-level quota hits zero, the system attempts to count against tenant burst credits; tenant credits depleted and resulted in opaque 429s with no retry_after header in some paths. This aligns with customer's "route_quota_exhausted" header in responses.
Dedicate pool config review: customer had not enabled 'separate-burst-pools' per traffic-class and had default smoothing enabled; no priority lane was configured for webhooks.
Related internal note: INT-330 has recent changes to burst-pool allocation for dedicated clusters — cross-checked to ensure current release isn't causing attribution bugs (no bug found).
resolution: Workaround applied by customer (temporary): reduced warmup concurrency from 50 -> 12 and added 300-800ms jitter across workers; webhooks moved to priority class with isolated burst pool. Result: webhook 429s dropped significantly on next run.

Permanent recommendations to be delivered: 1) configure route isolation for realtime webhook endpoints (isolated burst pool + higher priority weight); 2) reserve a small guaranteed capacity for webhook priority lane in dedicated pool config; 3) schedule heavy warmups outside critical webhook windows or use low-priority traffic class for warmup pins; 4) avoid reusing ephemeral keys across warmup worker fanouts (use one-time short-lived keys per worker or reuse a single long-lived warmup key to avoid fanout amplification).

Follow-up actions: Support to produce a short guidance doc with sample dedicated-pool snippets and recommended default values. SRE to add a dashboard tile for dedicated tenants showing burst-pool utilization and per-route exhaustion events. Owner: Marco Ruiz. ETA for docs: 2026-03-20.
Ticket status: awaiting delivery of guidance doc (will close after doc published and customer confirms).
